sections.heading: What Happens If You Just Pay an El Paso Speeding Ticket
paragraphs: Most people treat a speeding ticket like a parking fine — mail in the money and move on. In Texas that payment is a plea of guilty or no contest, and the court reports the conviction to the Department of Public Safety. The violation then sits on the driving record insurers pull at renewal time. A traffic conviction may affect insurance premiums depending on the driver's history, carrier and other rating factors, and that increase can run for several renewal cycles — which is how a "cheap" ticket quietly costs far more than the fine.

Convictions also stack. Texas no longer uses the former Driver Responsibility Program points system, but repeated moving-violation convictions can still affect a driver's record and may lead to a DPS license suspension in some circumstances. If you were cited for 25 mph or more over the limit, or for speeding in a school zone, many El Paso judges will not offer defensive driving at all — which makes having a lawyer negotiate the case the practical way to keep it off your record.

The good news: speeding is a Class C misdemeanor, the court has wide discretion, and these cases are resolved by negotiation on every docket. You just need someone who knows which prosecutor, which judge and which docket to ask.

sections.heading: Where a Speeding Case Can Go: Four Results We Negotiate For
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance with the court right away. That stops the clock on your appearance date and any failure-to-appear warrant, and from that point the court communicates with our office, not you.

We then pull the citation, the officer's notes and, where it exists, the radar or lidar calibration record. Many El Paso speeding tickets have fixable problems: a wrong statute number, an unposted or improperly posted limit, a device that was not calibrated on schedule, or an officer who is no longer with the department. Each of those is leverage. We present the case to the prosecutor on the next pretrial docket, and our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, driving record, court and circumstances.

sections.heading: Where Your Ticket Is: El Paso Municipal Court vs. County and Area Courts
paragraphs: Who wrote the ticket decides where it's filed. El Paso Police Department citations go to El Paso Municipal Court downtown. Tickets from the Sheriff's Office, a DPS state trooper on I-10 or Loop 375, or a constable go to one of the Justice of the Peace precincts. Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony each run their own municipal courts, and each has its own prosecutor and its own habits about deferrals.

Our flat fee covers the court your ticket is actually in: $59 for El Paso Municipal and $69 for JP and the smaller city courts. If you got more than one citation at the same stop — speeding plus no insurance, for example — each additional citation is handled at a discounted add-on rate shown on the checkout page. Not sure which court it is? Use the ticket and warrant lookup and we'll find it for you.

sections.heading: Fines, Court Costs and the Insurance Question
paragraphs: A Texas speeding fine is set by the court, up to a $200 maximum for most speeds, plus state and local court costs that the court adds on top. The exact total depends on the court and the speed. The old Driver Responsibility Program surcharges were repealed in 2019 and no longer apply; what remains is the conviction itself and what it does to your record. Our explainer on the former Texas points system covers what changed.

The lasting cost is insurance. Carriers re-rate at renewal, and a moving-violation conviction may raise premiums depending on your history and carrier. Against that, a flat $59 attorney fee aimed at avoiding the conviction is usually the more economical choice. It matters even more if you drive for work, hold a CDL, or already have recent convictions on your record.

sections.heading: Three Mistakes Drivers Make in the First Week
paragraphs: Check the appearance date printed on your citation — in El Paso Municipal Court it is often a couple of weeks out. Then avoid the three things that make a speeding case harder. Don't pay it, because payment is a plea. Don't request defensive driving yourself, because that request can lock you into a plea before anyone has looked at whether the ticket could simply be dismissed. Don't miss the date. If the date already passed, there may be a warrant; go to our warrant recall page and call us the same day. Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised.
Hire us before the appearance date and we take it from there. Our step-by-step guide to fighting a ticket in El Paso walks through what happens on the court side.

faqs.q: Is it worth hiring a lawyer for a speeding ticket in El Paso?
faqs.a: For many drivers, yes. Our fee is $59–$69 per ticket, and the outcomes we pursue — dismissal, deferred disposition or an amended charge — are aimed at keeping a conviction off your record. A conviction may affect insurance premiums for several years depending on your carrier and history, which is usually a larger cost than the fee.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court if I hire you?
faqs.a: Generally not for a speeding ticket in El Paso County. We appear on your behalf and handle the pretrial negotiation. You would only need to appear if the case were set for trial, which is uncommon and something we would discuss with you first.

faqs.q: Can you get a speeding ticket dismissed?
faqs.a: Sometimes — particularly when the citation has defects or the officer is unavailable. When an outright dismissal isn't available, deferred disposition reaches a similar practical result: the case is dismissed after a short deferral period and never becomes a conviction. No result can be promised in advance.

faqs.q: What if I was going 25+ mph over or in a school zone?
faqs.a: Those cases are harder because many courts won't offer defensive driving, but they are exactly where a lawyer matters most. We negotiate for deferred disposition or a reduced, non-moving charge so the high speed does not reach your record.

faqs.q: My appearance date already passed. Is it too late?
faqs.a: No, but act today. A missed date usually means a warrant and a separate Violate Promise to Appear charge. We can file an appearance, ask the court to recall the warrant and reset the case — see our traffic warrant recall page.

faqs.q: Does this apply to tickets from Horizon City, Socorro or the county?
faqs.a: Yes. We handle speeding tickets in El Paso Municipal Court, all El Paso County Justice of the Peace precincts, and the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony municipal courts.
